notes: Sweep 2026-10-23, skill condition: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every result.json records head d04061d with uncommitted false and skill_hash 005deae0a75971526e878940c13efb052c696a5b599949a07ecce352a8fc6e34, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the text graded here. Transcripts show Read calls on SKILL.md and references/ex_unit.md in all five and on references/processes.md in opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, not haiku-1 or haiku-2, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is met in 3 of 5. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since ba24972 (git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/): SKILL.md rewrote "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" and added three paragraphs to "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys"; references/ex_unit.md added one sentence (crash reports and the primary level) to "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler". None of these is in this case's index rows, so all eight graded rules are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-22-d standard.

Rewritten-rule bullets named by the caller (webhook-parser.md: required keys in the parsing head, no selecting pattern moved into a body, no unused field bound in every head of a 3+-clause function or in a spread head; library-client.md: no body re-match of one atom key or struct field, and the same head-binding bullet): those bullets belong to other cases and are not graded here, but none of their constructs occurs in these five files, so the count of runs violating each is 0 of 5. No run defines a multi-clause function (each TestMailer.deliver/2 and each test helper is one clause), and every body match is on a call's result, which the new "Read required keys" text keeps: {:registered_name, server} = Process.info(self(), :registered_name) (a literal), [{test_pid, _value}] = Registry.lookup(...), {:ok, _owner} = Registry.register(...).

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", per test name. opus-1 (10, all clean): 35 "adds a process to the topic's subscribers", 40 "adds an email address to the topic's subscribers", 45 "leaves the subscribers of other topics unchanged", 53 "returns an empty list for a topic without subscribers", 57 "returns the subscribers most recent first", 66 "sends the topic and payload to a subscribed process", 74 "mails each subscribed address with the topic in the subject", 83 "notifies only the subscribers of the published topic", 98 "removes the process from all its topics", 103 "keeps the other subscribers of its topics". haiku-1 (17, 1 violated): 34 "returns :ok for a pid" (VIOLATED: the body is only line 35: assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self()) == :ok), 38, 43, 48 "does not add the subscriber to other topics", 55, 59, 71, 77, 86 "does not mail a pid subscriber", 96, 102, 112, 123 "leaves the server running" (borderline, clean: it names an effect, as "does nothing for a topic without subscribers" has been graded), 130, 141, 151, 164 "fails to start without a :mailer". haiku-2 (14, all clean), including 109 "keeps the server running when the topic has no subscribers". sonnet-1 (15, all clean), including 119 "does nothing for a topic without subscribers" (borderline clean, as every earlier sweep). sonnet-2 (13, 1 violated): 108 "returns :ok for a topic nobody subscribed to" (VIOLATED: the same shape as 2026-10-22-d sonnet-1 line 94 "returns :ok for a topic without subscribers"; the body also asserts the topic stays empty, but the name says only that the call did not fail). Rule result: 2 of 5 violate (haiku-1, sonnet-2). No describe block joins two functions: haiku-1 splits publish/3 into "publish/3 to a pid subscriber", "to an email subscriber", "to a mix of subscribers" and "to a topic with no subscribers" (one function plus a condition) and adds "start_link/1"; sonnet-1 adds the condition "when an email subscriber is the only subscriber and a process exits elsewhere".

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`": haiku-1 is the only run testing a start failure, and line 166 is assert {:error, _reason} = start_supervised({Subscriptions, name: name}). It calls start_supervised/1 as the rule asks but leaves the reason open, so graded violated on the sentence "To assert that a start fails, call `start_supervised/1` and match the reason." and the rule's write half, which matches {:missing_mailer, _spec}. This shape has not been graded before (every earlier start-failure test matched {{%KeyError{key: :mailer}, _stacktrace}, _child}); it is a judgment call on a wildcard reason, by the same logic as the :DOWN sentence of "Wait for messages". No run calls start_link. Subscribers: opus-1 start_supervised!({Agent, ...}) stopped with stop_supervised!(Agent); the other four bare spawn/1 (clean as before).

"Wait for messages, not for time": every :DOWN pattern matches the reason the test caused: opus-1 line 116 :shutdown after stop_supervised!(Agent); haiku-1 line 181 :killed; haiku-2 line 171 :normal after send(pid, :stop); sonnet-1 lines 137 and 167 :killed; sonnet-2 line 143 :killed. Every refute_received follows a synchronous call (:sys.get_state/1 or subscribers/2) or an assert_receive; haiku-2 lines 105-106 and 113 use refute_receive with its timeout. No Process.sleep wait (sonnet-1 lines 129, 161 and sonnet-2 line 137 spawn(fn -> Process.sleep(:infinity) end) are subscriber bodies, not counted, as before), no Process.alive?.

The other graded rules are clean in 5 of 5. All five use async: true with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing test mailer that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! under that name and setup returns a map matched in test heads; no Process.register, application env, :meck or redefinition of Notify.Mailer. Every == has the call on the left; no elem/2, no bind-then-==; opus-1 line 99 and sonnet-1 line 143 refute <pid> in Subscriptions.subscribers(...) are membership checks graded clean, as 2026-10-22-d sonnet-2 line 166. Unmatched arrange calls (opus-1 lines 46, 58-59, 68-69, 75-77, 84-86, 110-112) are not matches and are clean, as haiku-2's unmatched publish calls were in 2026-10-22-d. Directive order: use then alias in all five (haiku-2 puts @registry after the aliases).
Not counted outside the list: nothing found. other_violations is empty in all five runs.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each: every run passed every time with no warnings (opus-1 10 tests, haiku-1 17, haiku-2 14, sonnet-1 15, sonnet-2 13). All five pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json. Against 2026-10-22-d (skill): opus clean on every rule again; haiku again has one :ok-only test name (haiku-1 line 34 now, haiku-2 line 64 then) and adds a Start processes violation (haiku-1 line 166, open start-failure reason); sonnet again has one :ok-only test name (sonnet-2 line 108 now, sonnet-1 line 94 then) and goes from violated to clean on Wait for messages.
